newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ coalition addendum reveals little of substance.
newsitem.headline: NZ coalition addendum reveals little of substance.

text.p: The National-New Zealand First government on Thursday released its addendum to the coalition agreement signed last week, but it contained little that was new or of significant fiscal impact.
The coalition agreed to fund up to NZ$200,000 in legal expenses for a possible class action against the UK government by New Zealand veterans of the Christmas Island nuclear tests.
A further $300,000 will be provided for the Commissioner for Children.
Otherwise the addendum contained a series of intentions and agreements in principle.

There was no mention of resourcing of nationalist New Zealand First, the junior partner in the coalition, despite claims by opposition Labour politicians that the issue had been raised at Labour's unsuccessful coalition negotiations with NZ First.
Labour deputy leader Michael Cullen said last week he believed an arrangement on resourcing had been struck but was being kept secret.
The supplement to the coalition deal showed the parties had agreed in principle that reserves of the Earthquake Commission should be adequate to meet substantial disasters.
They also agreed in principle to promote "expeditious implementation of the Commissioner's recommendations" in the "Winebox" investigation into alleged Cook Islands tax evasion schemes.
The parties agreed to consider establishing an independent commission against corruption after investigating whether existing criminal enforcement agencies and the existing law were adequate.
They also agreed to investigate whether those who had contracted hepatitis C and HIV from contaminated blood had received adequate compensation.
They agreed to encourage "by non-legislative means an increase in New Zealand-made programmes on television and radio".
